points.texte: The landscape on each card is made of hand-painted cardboard pieces in bright colours, with their brushstrokes and cardboard edges. Morning is blue and pink, afternoon orange, evening purple and pink, night deep blue.

The sky, the clouds, the distance, the middle ground and the foreground each slide at their own speed when you tilt the phone, and clouds drift slowly across the sky. Rare cards add trees or pillars on each side, like the wings of a theatre.

points.titre: The word's drawing becomes a plaque
points.texte: It is cut out of a thick plaque standing on a metal rod and base. Its material shows the rarity: mother-of-pearl for a common or uncommon card, silver for a rare one, gold for a very rare one. When you tilt the card, a gleam slides across the plaque.
Autumn leaves, petals, snowflakes and confetti are cut out of painted paper, and the summer birds perch on the clouds.

points.titre: The printed game's alley in colour
points.texte: Cards that come from the paper game stand in an alley with the colourful façades of the Grund, under a large gate hung with flowering ivy.
The next card is prepared in advance, exactly as it will appear.

images.alt: The “Bus” card, common, in the morning at the Rout Bréck, won in autumn, open and slowly tilted from left to right. The sky, the clouds, the distant city, the hills and the red bridge are pieces of cardboard painted in gouache, each sliding at its own speed; cardboard clouds cross the sky and paper leaves fall. The bus is a mother-of-pearl plaque on a metal rod and base: the plaque does not move, only a gleam slides across it.
images.legende: A common card being tilted: five painted layers, passing clouds, and the bus plaque with a sliding gleam.

images.alt: Four cards in the same alley, one after the other. 1. “Bank”, common: a blue and pink morning sky, a bank as a grey mother-of-pearl plaque. 2. “Chrëschtdag”, uncommon: an orange afternoon sky, a fir tree as a golden mother-of-pearl plaque. 3. “Brëll”, rare: a purple evening with lit windows, glasses as a silver plaque, pillars on the sides. 4. “Alphabet”, very rare: a deep blue night, three blocks A, B and C as a gold plaque. Each time, the alley with colourful façades under a large stone gate hung with flowering ivy. The screen is in French.
images.legende: Morning, afternoon, evening and night: the hour and the plaque material show the rarity.

images.alt: Four common cards in the Mëllerdall, between the sandstone rocks, one after the other. 1. “Bam”, won in winter: snow on the ridges and paper snowflakes. 2. “Hand”, in spring: flowers in the hills and falling petals. 3. “Café”, in summer: birds perched on the clouds. 4. “Kapp”, in autumn: russet foliage and brightly coloured paper leaves.
images.legende: The season of the day the card was won, in painted paper.

points.titre: Each card's drawing fills the whole window
points.texte: The cat, the house, the bus or the digit of a number card are now much bigger and centred in the window, with the landscape setting them off all around. Every card in the collection benefits, open or in the grid.
The ribbon that follows the sound of the word is taller and thicker.

images.alt: Two columns, “Before” and “After”. At the top, the Mäi Carnet grid with six cards: Kaz, Bus, Haus, dräi, Fliger, Päerd. Before, the cat, the bus, the house, the 3, the plane and the horse are small in the middle of their landscape; after, each one fills its window. At the bottom, the open Bus card: before, a small bus at the bottom of the window; after, a large bus spanning its whole width. The screen is in French.
images.legende: Each card's drawing now fills the whole window.

points.titre: A new series in the collection: Level A1
points.texte: The 800 or so A1-level words listed by the official Luxembourgish dictionary, sorted by theme (family, jobs, food and drink, health, months and holidays…), then verbs, adjectives and little words. Each empty slot shows the meaning of the word to find.

points.titre: The games help you fill it
points.texte: After the essentials, Wuertsich, Wuertmix and Wuertriet slip into their games the A1 words still missing from your collection.

images.alt: Mäi Carnet, Series view. Under the title “Level A1”, the “Family” page, 1 of 31: the Famill card is won, the other empty slots show the meaning of the word to find: granny, grandpa, boy, brother, cousin, daughter, parents, grandson, granddaughter, wife, grandmother, grandfather, child, mother, mum, man. The screen is in French.
images.legende: The Level A1 series in the collection: the family page.

points.titre: The tab on printed cards hangs from a chain
points.texte: The small reminder of the type and the cost, under the Strength, hangs from the badge by a chain that follows the rarity: a big iron ring for a common card, two bronze links, three silver links, and a gold chain with a pearl for a very rare one.

images.alt: The corner of four printed cards, from least to most rare. Under the Strength badge hangs a tab repeating the type and the cost. 1. Common, iron: one big ring. 2. Uncommon, bronze: two links. 3. Rare, silver: three thin links. 4. Very rare, gold: two links and a purple pearl.
images.legende: The chain of the tab follows the rarity of the printed card.

points.texte: The “zweeavéierzeg” card shows a big 42 in the middle of its landscape, in mother-of-pearl like the other drawings. You recognise each number at a glance in the collection, and on the printed card too.

images.alt: Three open number cards. 1. “siwen”, iron: a big pearly 7 in front of the castle. 2. “zweeavéierzeg”, gold: a big golden 42 in front of the city at night. 3. “honnert”, iron: a big 100 in front of the castle. The cards are in French.
images.legende: Each number card shows its number in large figures.
